main_text.p: cium absoluat. Est autem iustum precium, quod saltem veri precii partem dimidiam adæquat. verum autē, quan-ti communi hominum æsti-matione res est. quare ut suppleat emptor, unum addere debebit. His positis, quæro vicissim de emptore hoc mo-do: Titius equum decem aureorum, emit sexdecim. Re cognita, queritur, se ultra dimidium rei precium fraudatum: &,ut venditio rescinda-tur, petit. nam venditoris ea-dem, quæ emptoris, ratio ef-se debet. At vēditor tum erat deceptus, cum rei precium e-rat amplius dimidio diminu-tum:

page.notes: The left margin carries a handwritten-looking mark (a pen-drawn hand or flourish) beside the first lines. It is not printed text and is left out. A small stroke mark stands below the last line, under "tum:". It is not a catchword and is left out. The running head shows "TIT." followed by a heavy decorative word that I could not read, so it is marked illegible. "vēditor" is read from "uéditor" with an abbreviation stroke; the reading is doubtful. "precij" is read as "precii", with the final letter a vowel.
